assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin biology is a rare chain from basic hormone physiology to transformative therapy: GLP-1 as a glucose-dependent insulin secretagogue and satiety signal, then long-acting analogues that reshape diabetes and obesity care. Originality and lasting clinical and physiological impact are both very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over several groups (Habener, Mojsov, Holst, Drucker, Knudsen and others). Drucker and Holst established the physiology and the intestinotropic and secretory roles; Mojsov's peptide-chemistry contribution is contested in priority terms. Knudsen's industrial analogue work is decisive for the drug but fits a three-person cap awkwardly.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of replication, large cardiovascular and weight-loss outcome trials, and wide clinical adoption. Timing is strong.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen (and uncredited Habener) is unresolved.
Whether the committee prefers physiology or drug development is uncertain; my knowledge of priority disputes is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality. The concept, receptor design and clinical proof are clearly important and original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs) and June (4-1BB CARs and clinical translation) are central; Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials are foundational. Eshhar's earlier chimeric receptor concept and Brentjens, Kalos and others complicate a clean trio.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy in haematological cancers; solid tumours, toxicity and durability remain open. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Eshhar's priority is not among the credited names, so the trio may be incomplete.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and long-term safety are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type-specific control of excitable cells with light, transforming neuroscience experimentation. Channelrhodopsin identification and its neuronal deployment form a clear, original and heavily used invention.
assessment.attribution: Bamberg and Nagel (with Hegemann) characterised channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenböck proposed and first demonstrated genetically targeted photoactivation. Six credited names exceed three slots; my choice favours the channel discovery plus the neuronal demonstration, but this is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Extremely widely replicated and entrenched in research, though therapeutic translation is still early (retinal applications). Recognition is mature on the tool side.
uncertainties: Choice among Hegemann, Boyden and Miesenböck versus the proposed three is contested.
Impact is primarily on research tools rather than direct medicine; committee weighting is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide therapy for SMA (nusinersen) is a mechanism-driven, RNA-processing-based treatment that turned a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one. Clear conceptual originality in correcting SMN2 exon 7 splicing and strong clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the exon 7 splicing regulation and the ISS-N1 target concept with collaborators, and Bennett led antisense chemistry and clinical development at Ionis. Contributions of Singh, Hua, Adrian Krainer's collaborators and the SMN gene discovery by Melki and others may need acknowledgement; the two-person configuration seems fair.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with multi-year outcome data and follow-on RNA therapeutics validating the approach; timing is good.
uncertainties: Wider antisense field (e.g. Zamecnik, Stephenson) and gene-therapy comparators complicate credit.
Long-term outcomes across patient ages are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defines a new intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus, with the Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) splicing mechanism and downstream roles in disease. A classic, clean and original discovery with lasting impact in cell biology and disease.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily identified the UPR transducers and the unconventional mRNA splicing mechanism; a two-person award is a natural fit. Others (Ron, Kaufman, Shamu) contributed to branches of the pathway.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed over three decades with broad relevance to disease (diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer), though the direct medical application is less mature than some other candidates.
uncertainties: Contributions of Ron and Kaufman (PERK/ATF6 branches) may be argued as decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV cancers, with population-level reductions in disease. The VLP technology is original and the public-health impact is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs, and Frazer (with Zhou) contributed the VLP expression and vaccine development. Zhou's early death and the parallel Georgetown/Rochester work (Kirnbauer, Rose) complicate credit; zur Hausen was recognised in 2008 for HPV-cancer link.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with strong evidence of effectiveness from national vaccination programmes, so recognition is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation with Jian Zhou, Kirnbauer and Georgetown groups is contested.
Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the 2008 HPV recognition is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING reveals how cytosolic DNA triggers type I interferon and inflammation, linking infection, autoimmunity and cancer immunity. A conceptually clean and important mechanism with broad biological reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide cGAMP second messenger; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING. Burdette and Vance on cyclic dinucleotide binding and Sun/Wu coauthors on cGAS also contributed; a Chen-Barber-Ishikawa trio is a plausible, but not unique, configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism strongly confirmed, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has been disappointing so far; recognition may be somewhat early for medicine impact.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is weak so far.
Boundaries of credit between STING identification groups (Barber, Ishikawa, Glen, Zhu and others) are not fully clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating TNF as a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis converted cytokine biology into a major class of anti-inflammatory biologics, transforming rheumatology and inflammatory bowel disease care.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the proof-of-concept work in human synovial cultures and clinical trials; the credited pair is coherent. Contributions from Cerami, Beutler (TNF identification) and the anti-TNF antibody developers could be considered by the committee.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of clinical use and biosimilars; timing is late rather than early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the TNF discovery and antibody engineering contributions of others.
Novelty relative to many later biologics may be viewed as less fundamental.
